text:
Alexis Lafrenière has 10 goals in 23 games, and he's finally playing like the first overall pick everyone waited on. Sports Illustrated said he looks like a star a quarter into the season; The Hockey News wrote about him becoming a multi-dimensional player.

Our numbers like the player and are wary of the shooting. He's scoring on 19.6% of his shots, against a talent range that tops out around 17%, and he has 1.9 more goals than his chances deserve. The last ten games have been quieter, one goal and seven points, and that's probably closer to normal than the first dozen were.

What is real is the two-way game. Evolving-Hockey had him 29th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season, taking chances away against top competition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 57% of his shots coming off the rush, so he does his damage in the seconds after a turnover.

Wins added has him 51st in the league, with his goals swinging games more than most. What to watch: shot volume. At 51 through 23 games, more shots is the way to keep the goals coming once the percentage settles.
